item.content:encoded:
I'm actually not a big fan of this one. It could be that anatomy and biology were always a roadblock for me, but I just can't enjoy this one. I'm glad Dexanote mentioned in a previous post that all instances created by 646 were actual creatures that existed on Earth at one point. It would have been cool if this thing had actually given birth to other SCPs, but as long as the rule has been established then it's fine and I can't really demean it.

However, aside from the small editorial mistakes, I, like others have mentioned, feel as though the expunged portions were grouped too closely together. If this were truly random, I'd expect more unknown variables early on.

I also wanted to run this across the original author and any other of the writers or staff that may be looking at this, and didn't want to be presumptuous and change it. But…

SCP-646 is constantly producing unrelated, infant organisms. For the purposes of this document, SCP-646 is in a state of "giving birth".

It took me until the experiment log to realize that it was constantly giving birth. I just feel that this should be phrased differently as it made me think that the offspring merely had different or mixed DNA; as if it weren't directly related to 646 despite being birthed by it and being the same species. I suggest something more along the lines of…

For the purposes of this article, SCP-646 is in a constant state of parturition, giving birth to genealogically unrelated infants in both genus and species.

…or something similar. Not real happy how that sounds either.

Lastly, the reproduction rate. Seriously?! Seriously, is that how fast it goes?! Do they have an on-site vet at all times? Are they euthanizing? If they are, that seems like an overuse, and possible waste, of Foundation resources. It would be easier just to have SCP-646 next to a furnace or an incinerator as an effective means of getting rid of any offspring.

Unfortunately, this all means a -1 from me. Even if the passage that I had previously mentioned had been rewritten, the reproduction rate seems too unrealistic, even for SCP Foundation standards. Sorry, as it appears that a lot of staff and writers like this one.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made by author as described below.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

Alright, so this one is definitely a weird article, and the fact that none of the animals birthed by SCP-646 are anomalous kind rules out a lot of potential crosslinks there. However, an easy, and non-intrusive way in which to link in other SCPs, especially animal SCPs, would be to update the log so that those animals are taken for use in the further study of those anomalous objects. As such, I am proposing the following additions to the log table:

Add the following two logs:
XX:XX Corvus corax Common Raven Taken for use in ongoing SCP-1505 research.
XX:XX Mammuthus primigenius Woolly Mammoth Retained for study. Genetic material collected for SCP-2082 research.

I have left the times intentionally blank, as it would be best to disperse these through out the log rather than cluster them.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
Piecewise, I agree with your idea of this being a DNA one-armed bandit. The other thing I have a problem with is that 646 seems to generate much more biomass than would be accounted for by its daily allotment of 10kg of food. I think a birthrate of several per day instead of some 200 or so would make a lot more sense. Can you imagine the amount of personnel and resources needed to analyze and handle that many offspring? Especially if one of them turns out to be dangerous in some way?

Also, since it is clearly possible to generate sapient creatures, I think a follow-up would be critical to giving hints at the nature of 646, or at least make the article more interesting. What happened to human female? Did she survive? Did she develop normally? What happened when she learned to speak?

As it is, there really isn't much to make this SCP interesting and definitely nothing to make it seem dangerous or scary, despite the obvious avenues for something really disturbing or threatening.

There should be at least one offspring in the log that is difficult to contain, or exhibits some dangerous characteristic. This would provide a good reason for the Foundation to maintain the expenditures needed to analyze, categorize and possibly maintain hundreds of new creatures a day.

Perhaps one day it delivers a nasty little lizard-like creature that is surprisingly hard to terminate…
